title: Shorter Skills briefs
reader_summary: Write Skills blurbs with stricter rules: one sentence per section when we can, and exactly one “try this” step — no invented architecture.
outcome_line: Kept. Treatment cut output ~18% with 13/13 rubric pass and stronger Why-now scores on average.
how_we_measure: We compare how long the blurbs are (cost) and whether they still name real features, give one useful next step, and cite a timely hook. Clicks are not part of this test.

reader_glossary.meaning: A GitHub tool that turns a codebase into a knowledge graph so an AI can look up facts in order, instead of getting one dump. We did not install it. We copied the habit: README first (what the repo does), news last, and only for the “why now” line.

A skill for coding agents that fights overbuilding — use the built-in date field, not a date-picker library. We did not install it, and this is not a test of the Ponytail skill that often appears on the Skills list. We copied the habit: one thing to try, no invented architecture.
An old proverb: You Aren't Gonna Need It. Don't add extra layers “just in case.” Ponytail is YAGNI for agents. For this digest it means: don't recommend a three-tool stack the README never mentioned.

hypothesis: If we give Claude the README first and the news last, and we tell it to keep each Skills blurb short with exactly one thing to try, the write-ups should get more specific and more useful — and about 10% cheaper — without losing a real reason the repo is timely.
change_summary: On Skills only: ordered prompt (README, then metadata, then web/HN) plus tighter writing rules (short sections, one try-this step, no invented architecture).
verdict: Baseline (14 Skills runs, 2026-08-03→2026-08-16, flags off): mean 2005 output tokens and 1239 words per run; rank-1 rubric 14/14 pass (100%); why_now avg 3.4/5; specificity avg 5.0/5. Treatment (13 Skills runs, 2026-08-17→2026-08-29, DIGEST_NARRATE_STRUCTURED_CONTEXT=1 + DIGEST_NARRATE_PONYTAIL=1): mean 1649 output tokens (−17.8%) and 1026 words (−17.2%) per run; rank-1 rubric 13/13 pass (100%); why_now avg 4.1/5 (+0.7); specificity avg 4.5/5 (−0.5, still passes). Editorial spot-check: Why-now lines still cite timely hooks (HN, GitHub Trending, v2.0 releases) on treatment briefs; four late-window rank-1 picks scored why_now=2 on star-velocity phrasing but passed rubric and retained real hooks elsewhere in the digest. PostHog out of scope per experiment notes. **Keep** both structured-context and ponytail flags on the Skills digest command.
